difficulty.from: engine meta: 2 straight folds, 2 punches, 4 holes

answer.line: Unfold in reverse. Fold 2 adds no holes; fold 1 mirrors the top row into the bottom row. Four holes in the two right columns.

steps: Work backward. Undo the last fold first, and mirror any hole on its flap across that crease.
Undo fold 2, the left strip folded over. The punches are in the two right columns, which that strip never covered. Nothing new: still 2 holes, top row.
Undo fold 1, the bottom half folded up. Both layers were punched, so each top-row hole gets a partner in the bottom row, the same distance from the crease.
Final sheet: 4 holes, top and bottom rows, in the two right columns.

choices.display: two left columns, top and bottom rows
choices.note: The answer's pattern, mirrored left to right. The punches sat on the right side of the folded paper, and nothing moves them left.
The answer's pattern turned a quarter turn: its two columns became two rows.

choices.display: two right columns, top and bottom rows
choices.note: Fold 2 adds nothing; fold 1 mirrors the top row into the bottom row.
Two ways land here: mirroring across the fold 2 crease, which adds nothing, or leaving fold 1 closed. Fold 1 opens across its own crease and doubles the holes.

choices.display: four holes, one in the third row
choices.note: A mirrored hole sits as far below the crease as the original sits above it. Top row maps to bottom row, not the third row.

lockIt: Unfold in reverse. Each unfold mirrors the holes on its flap across the crease; holes off the flap stay single.
